t: Section 302 of the Public Works and Economic Development Act of 1965 (42 U.S.C. 3152) is amended by striking out “and June 30, 1971” and inserting in lieu thereof “June 30, 1971, June 30, 1972, and June 30, 1973”.

fable.w: This section only amends an existing statute to extend fiscal-year dates, apparently an authorization period, through 1972 and 1973. The tempting reading is that the underlying Public Works and Economic Development Act involves state and local planning, but this text itself establishes no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: is amended by striking out “and June 30, 1971” and inserting in lieu thereof “June 30, 1971, June 30, 1972, and June 30, 1973”

opus.w: This amendment only replaces "and June 30, 1971" with a longer list of fiscal-year dates in Section 302. It sets up no process for anyone outside the federal government to take part in a decision. Even if the underlying program involves grants, applying for grants does not count as participation, and nothing here adds consultation, a hearing or rulemaking.
opus.b: The obvious reading is the right one here. The section only changes dates in the Public Works and Economic Development Act. The underlying section 302 may involve planning grants. But this amendment adds no consultation, hearing, advisory body, comment period or right to sue, so no one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment that extends a deadline date in another statute. It does not establish any mechanism for public comment, consultation with outside entities, public hearings, or advisory committees. It involves no interaction with parties outside the federal government regarding a decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: Section 302 of the Public Works and Economic Development Act of 1965 (42 U.S.C. 3152) is amended by striking out “and June 30, 1971” and inserting in lieu thereof “June 30, 1971, June 30, 1972, and June 30, 1973”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that extending the deadline for a program implicitly involves public participation if the program itself involves grants or contracts. However, the text provided is merely a technical amendment to a date. It does not describe any process of consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory board involvement. It is a legislative housekeeping provision.
